customer.business: ChefJiw (a Thai cooking-coach phone app, freemium)
customer.target: Thai home cooks in Thailand, 20 to 45, who cook simple Thai dishes at home at least a few times a week and use a smartphone. Incomes are shown in US dollars; the app's prices are in Thai baht.

segments.name: Young worker in Bangkok learning to cook (about 18,000-40,000 baht a month)
Parent cooking for a family in a city outside Bangkok (about 15,000-35,000 baht a month)
University student living alone (about 4,000-10,000 baht a month, mostly allowance)
Mid-career professional who cooks on weekends (about 45,000-90,000 baht a month)

behaviours.name: Street-food regular
behaviours.how: Eats out or orders delivery most days because a plate costs 50-60 baht; cooks only when there is time.

behaviours.name: Learns from free videos
behaviours.how: Watches YouTube or TikTok cooking clips and follows along on the phone.

behaviours.name: Cooks to save money
behaviours.how: Cooks at home to spend less, compares prices, avoids subscriptions.

behaviours.name: Asks family
behaviours.how: Calls mum or follows family recipes; trusts people more than apps.

behaviours.name: App tryer
behaviours.how: Downloads new apps when friends share them and deletes them fast if they do not help.

behaviours.name: Uses a free AI chat app
behaviours.how: Already asks a general AI assistant for recipes and cooking help, for free.

behaviours.name: Health-focused cook
behaviours.how: Cooks at home to control oil, salt and calories.

pitch:
ChefJiw, a Thai cooking app for iPhone and Android, in Thai or English. All prices are in Thai baht.
Chef Elephant walks you through a dish one step at a time on your phone: what to do now, how high the heat should be, a timer, and what to look for. Big buttons for messy hands, and the screen stays on. Stuck? Tap "Ask the chef" (3 typed questions a day, free).
Free to try: basil pork with fried egg, and green curry from paste, the dish people most often get wrong from a video, so you can see if the chef does better before you pay anything.
The 12-dish pack, 99 baht once, yours to keep, no subscription: 12 more dishes most home cooks can't make from memory (such as tom yum, pad see ew and massaman). Every dish is cooked by home cooks before it goes live, and most need only one pan. If a dish doesn't come out right, tap "It didn't work" and the chef goes through the step with you.
The pack includes 4 Sunday cook-ahead plans: three dishes that keep all week, one shopping list, and what the week costs per meal at market prices, next to buying a 50-baht plate.
More packs come later, each sold separately.
